notes:
I wasn't able to research Joel 1, so I have no commentary notes to give you.

My first attempt tried to open eight pages at once (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit on Bible Hub, Wesley's notes on StudyLight, New Advent and GotQuestions). It hit the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with fewer pages, I had no tool calls left for this turn. None of the pages loaded, so I read nothing.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say, with a URL for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no source text, any verse notes I wrote now would come from memory and break those rules.

**What to do next:** ask me again in a new message. I'll load the sources one or two at a time so I stay within the limit, in this order:
1. **The traditional reading of each verse:** enduringword.com (Joel 1), preceptaustin.org (Joel 1), and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu or studylight.org), Spurgeon or Desiring God, and a Reformed or Lutheran source. I'll focus on the main debates: whether the locusts in v. 4 and v. 6 are real insects or invading armies, and what "the Day of the LORD" in v. 15 means.
3. **Other views:** netbible.org translator notes, bibleodyssey.org, and Catholic or Orthodox readings from newadvent.org, catholic.com or oca.org. I'll only include these where the pages actually say something.

If you'd rather get results faster, you could ask for one section at a time, starting with the traditional reading of each verse.
